<summary>Existing env contract tests still target `run.ts`</summary>

**Cause:** The PR moved `buildSharedEnv()` from `.agent/src/run.ts` into `.agent/src/runtime-env.ts`, but `.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts` still reads `run.ts` and asserts that secondary-token and reasoning-effort env wiring appears there. The live `Test Scripts` run fails on `shared run-agent-task exposes an optional secondary GitHub token` and `run-agent-task maps reasoning effort for Claude env and Codex thought level`.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the old source-contract assertions to inspect `runtime-env.ts`, or better, add direct `buildSharedEnv()` behavioral coverage in `.agent/src/__tests__/runtime-env.test.ts` for `INPUT_SECONDARY_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, while preserving the action/workflow wiring checks in `envelope.test.ts`.

**Comments:** This is not a design objection to the extraction. It is a required test update because the current PR head has a failing required check.

</details>

@sepo-agent /answer one last check -- search the acpx documentation and make sure the way we set the enviable is aligned with their specs (also make sure the version is correct) . please provide reference links

Checked. The env var setup in PR #363 is aligned with ACPX’s auth spec.

- ACPX says ACP `authenticate` uses config `auth` entries or `ACPX_AUTH_<METHOD_ID>` env vars; ambient vars like `OPENAI_API_KEY` are passed through but do not select auth by themselves: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/docs/CLI.md#config-command
- PR #363 keeps `OPENAI_API_KEY` and mirrors it to `ACPX_AUTH_OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ACPX_AUTH_CODEX_API_KEY`, which matches that convention: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4d80ce9aea33de93d1bf584087c77c79a45ed929/.agent/src/runtime-env.ts#L1-L40
- Codex ACP docs list both `CODEX_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` auth methods, so covering both aliases is reasonable: https://github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp#readme

Version check: the repo currently locks `acpx` to `0.6.1` via `.agent/package-lock.json`, with `^0.6.1` in `.agent/package.json`. That version is compatible with this fix because ACPX v0.6.0 is where explicit `ACPX_AUTH_*` / config auth selection was introduced for this behavior: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#2026425-v060

One caveat: npm currently reports `acpx` latest as `0.10.0`, and ACPX’s changelog lists `2026.5.23 (v0.10.0)`: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#2026523-v0100. So the PR is correct for the installed version, but the dependency is not latest. I would treat an `acpx` bump as a separate follow-up because v0.9.0 changed the default Codex adapter path/model handling.

For `acpx` 0.9.0, the important change is model handling: the default Codex adapter switches to `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`, and Codex model selection is handled through adapter-advertised ACP model IDs. ACPX’s CLI docs also say `--model <id>` now expects an agent-supported model path: non-Claude agents must advertise ACP models and support model setting, otherwise ACPX fails clearly instead of silently falling back.

Best practice for fixing that is:

1. Keep PR #363’s auth fix as-is for the current `0.6.1` line.
2. Treat an `acpx` 0.9+ upgrade as a separate compatibility PR.
3. In that PR, make Sepo’s Codex `model` value an ACP adapter model ID, not a guessed OpenAI API model name.
4. For persistent sessions, prefer ACPX’s model operation path: `acpx codex set model <id>` / `session/set_model`.
5. Keep `reasoning_effort` separate unless the new adapter explicitly folds reasoning into the advertised model ID.
6. Add a smoke test around the exact generated ACPX commands for Codex session setup, model setting, and thought/reasoning setting.

Downsides of upgrading to `acpx` 0.9.0:

- It changes the built-in Codex adapter from the older Zed adapter path to `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#2026522-v090
- Model IDs may change or become stricter. Existing Sepo `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` values that worked as raw Codex names could fail if they are not advertised ACP model IDs.
- Session continuity may reset because ACPX session scoping includes the agent command; changing the built-in adapter command can create a different session scope.
- Auth method IDs should be revalidated against the new adapter. `ACPX_AUTH_OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ACPX_AUTH_CODEX_API_KEY` are still the right pattern, but the supported method IDs are adapter-owned.
- It increases blast radius: lockfile, docs, tests, session setup, model policy, and possibly retry/failure handling all need a full pass.

References:
- ACPX 0.9.0 change note: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#2026522-v090
- ACPX `--model` behavior: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/docs/CLI.md#global-options
- ACPX `set model` behavior: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/docs/CLI.md#set-command
- Current ACPX Codex examples: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx/blob/main/README.md#usage-examples
